textRun.content: The Historical & Modern Therapeutics of Disease Nomenclature
A Sister Manuscript Tracking Treatment Evolution from Time of Discovery to Present Day
This volume serves as a companion manuscript to
. While the first manuscript traces the biological and naming chain (
American Name → Disease → Symptomology → Bacteria → Fungi/Yeast/Mold → Immunoglobulins → Serotyping → Virus
for each of the 53 disease entities.
For each entry, treatments are tracked chronologically across three eras:
Bloodletting, herbal emetics, counter-irritants, heavy metals (mercury, arsenic), and primitive isolations.
Development of antitoxins, early chemical magic bullets, targeted antibiotics, and immunization programs.
Contemporary antimicrobial regimens, antiviral therapies, modern supportive care, and clinical protocols.
Sanatorium rest cure, alpine air therapy, cod liver oil, bloodletting, gold salts, counter-irritant chest plasters, and therapeutic pneumothorax (collapsing the lung).
Streptomycin (1943), Para-aminosalicylic acid (PAS), Isoniazid (1952), Rifampicin (1965), and BCG vaccination.
Multi-drug therapy regimen (Rifampin, Isoniazid, Pyrazinamide, Ethambutol - RIPE protocol); specialized regimens for MDR-TB and XDR-TB incorporating Bedaquiline and Linezolid.
Inhalations of creosote or tar vapors, opium preparations for cough suppression, milk diets, and cauterization.
Surgical thoracoplasty, streptomycin, isoniazid, and ethambutol.
Standard 6-month combination antibiotic protocol (RIPE regimen) with directly observed therapy (DOT).
The "Royal Touch" (monarchs touching the scrofulous swellings), topical iodine tinctures, surgical excision of swollen neck glands, and poultices.
Surgical debridement combined with early anti-tuberculous chemotherapy.
First-line systemic anti-TB pharmacotherapy (RIPE) for 6 months; surgical excision reserved strictly for refractory or suppurative cases.
Cold ice packs applied to the shaved scalp, aggressive venesection (bloodletting), leeching behind the ears, mercury subchloride (calomel), and lumbar punctures for fluid decompression.
Flexner’s antimeningococcal serum (1907), Sulfonamides (1930s), Penicillin G (1940s), and polysaccharide vaccines.
High-dose intravenous third-generation cephalosporins (Ceftriaxone or Cefotaxime) plus Vancomycin, adjunctive Dexamethasone, and conjugated meningococcal vaccines (MenACWY / MenB).
Cupping, venesection, antimony emetics, mustard plasters applied to the chest, and turpentine stupes.
Type-specific antipneumococcal serum therapy (1910s–1930s), Sulfapyridine (M&B 693), Penicillin, and 23-valent polysaccharide vaccines (PPSV23).
Beta-lactam antibiotics (Amoxicillin or Ceftriaxone) combined with Macrolides (Azithromycin) or respiratory Fluoroquinolones; Pneumococcal Conjugate Vaccines (PCV15/PCV20).
Chapter 2: Throat Disorders and Severe Febrile Plagues
Caustic silver nitrate swabbed onto the throat membrane, tracheotomy without anesthesia, blow-pipes with powdered alum, and lime-water inhalations.
Behring & Kitasato’s Diphtheria Antitoxin (DAT) (1890s), Diphtheria Toxoid immunization (Ramon, 1920s), and Penicillin/Erythromycin.
Immediate administration of Equine Diphtheria Antitoxin (DAT), IV Erythromycin or Penicillin G, strict respiratory isolation, and DTaP/Tdap vaccination protocols.
Gargles of port wine and bark (quinine), gargling with vinegar and salt, external blister packs applied to the neck.
High-dose equine antitoxin neutralization and systemic penicillin therapy.
Early antitoxin administration, intensive care airway management, and targeted antibacterial therapy.
Manual scraping or mechanical removal of pseudomembranes using forceps, emetics to induce violent vomiting to clear airways.
Intubation, diphtheria antitoxin, and parenteral penicillin.
Airway maintenance via endotracheal intubation, DAT neutralization, and systemic antibiotics.
Steam tents, croup kettles, emetic syrup of ipecac, and throat lancing.
O'Dwyer intubation tubes, diphtheria antitoxin, nebulized epinephrine, and corticosteroids.
Dexamethasone, nebulized racemic epinephrine, diphtheria antitoxin (if diphtheritic), and supportive oxygenation.
Peruvian Cinchona bark powder, raw Quinine extraction, Fowler’s solution (arsenic), and draining of swamp vapors (miasma theory).
Synthetic Chloroquine, Primaquine, Mepacrine, and vector control (DDT spraying).
Artemisinin-based Combination Therapies (ACTs - e.g., Artemether-Lumefantrine), IV Artesunate for severe malaria, and RTS,S/R21 malaria vaccines.
Chapter 3: Enteric, Vector-Borne, and Spirocheta Infections
Calomel (mercury), purgatives, cold sponges, turpentine stupes applied to the abdomen, and liquid whey diets.
Wright’s killed typhoid vaccine (1896), Chloramphenicol (1948), and Ampicillin.
Fluoroquinolones (Ciprofloxacin), Ceftriaxone, or Azithromycin; Typhoid Vi conjugate vaccines; supportive rehydration.
12. Jail Fever / Camp Fever / Ship Fever
Jail fever / camp fever / ship fever
Delousing with vinegar/kerosene, ventilation, isolation, wine and camphor stimulants, and vinegar-soaked rags on the forehead.
DDT louse powder delousing, Tetracycline (1950s), and Chloramphenicol.
Oral or IV Doxycycline; strict vector/louse control hygiene measures.
Cauterization of bite wounds with boiling oil or red-hot iron, madstones applied to the wound, and restraint.
Pasteur’s live-attenuated spinal cord vaccine (1885), Duck embryo vaccine, and Human Rabies Immune Globulin (HRIG).
Immediate wound washing, Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP) combining Human Rabies Immune Globulin (HRIG) on Day 0 and 4 doses of modern cell-culture Rabies Vaccine.
14. French Pox / Bad Blood / Great Pox
French pox / bad blood / great pox
Mercury inunctions (salivation therapy), mercury vapor baths, guaiacum wood infusions, and "fever therapy" (malariotherapy - Wagner-Jauregg).
Ehrlich's Salvarsan / Arsphenamine (1910), Neosalvarsan, and Penicillin G (1943).
Parenteral Benzathine Penicillin G (single dose for early syphilis; weekly doses for late/latent syphilis); Doxycycline for penicillin-allergic patients.
Cauterization of dirty wounds, laudanum (opium) for spasms, chloral hydrate, and warm baths.
Tetanus Antitoxin (TAT) (1890), Tetanus Toxoid vaccine (1920s), curare muscle relaxants, and mechanical ventilation.
Human Tetanus Immune Globulin (HTIG), Tetanus Toxoid immunization (Tdap/Td), Metronidazole or Penicillin G, IV Diazepam/Magnesium sulfate for severe spasms, and surgical wound debridement.
Chapter 4: Viral Hemorrhagic Fevers, Paralysis, and Toxin Envenomation
Emetics, diaphoresis (inducing sweating), cinchona bark for pain, and bloodletting.
Oral rehydration therapy, intravenous fluids for Dengue Shock Syndrome, and Paracetamol (avoiding aspirin).
Isotonic IV fluid resuscitation, blood transfusion monitoring, avoidance of NSAIDs/aspirin, and Dengue vaccines (Dengvaxia/Qdenga).
Quinine pills, hot toddies (whiskey, honey, lemon), mustard plasters, Dover's powder (opium + ipecac), and bed rest.
Inactivated Influenza Vaccines (1940s), Amantadine (1960s), and Rimantadine.
Neuraminidase inhibitors (Oseltamivir/Zanamivir), Cap-dependent endonuclease inhibitors (Baloxavir marboxil), annual quadrivalent influenza vaccines.
18. American Plague / Yellow Jack / Bronze John / Dock Fever
American plague / yellow jack / bronze John / dock fever
Aggressive purging with calomel and jalap, venesection, quarantine of ships, mosquito smudges, and lemonade/barley water.
Max Theiler’s 17D live attenuated Yellow Fever Vaccine (1937) and supportive fluid therapy.
Supportive fluid management, treatment of coagulopathies and liver failure, and 17D single-dose vaccination.
Ice chips swallowed whole, stomach poultices, opiates, and turpentine enemata.
Blood transfusions, vitamin K, and IV fluids.
Critical care unit support, fresh frozen plasma/blood transfusions, renal dialysis, and hemodialysis.
Syrup of squill, belladonna extracts, change of air (mountain/sea air), and suffocating burning sulfur vapor baths.
Whole-cell pertussis vaccines (1930s), Erythromycin, and Acellular Pertussis vaccines (DTaP).
Macrolide antibiotics (Azithromycin or Clarithromycin) to clear nasal shedding; supportive oxygen/suctioning; DTaP/Tdap vaccination.
Splinting and immobilization of limbs, plaster casts, strychnine injections, and Sister Kenny's hot packs and passive range-of-motion physical therapy.
Drinker's Iron Lung respirator (1928), Salk's Inactivated Polio Vaccine (IPV, 1955), and Sabin's Oral Polio Vaccine (OPV, 1961).
Preventive immunization (IPV/OPV), non-invasive positive pressure ventilation, physical therapy, and orthopedic corrective management.
This complementary manuscript establishes the parallel history of therapeutics across all 53 disease entities, aligning with the biological classifications defined in
